recipes.name: Pineapple Grilled Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) can pineapple rings, juice drained and reserved

steps.text: Mix together the drained pineapple juice, brown sugar, soy sauce, and garlic powder together in a large plastic zipper bag, and smush the bag a few times with your hands to mix the marinade and dissolve the sugar. Place the pork chops into the marinade, squeeze out any air in the bag, seal it, and refrigerate overnight. Reserve the pineapple rings.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat, and lightly oil the grate.

Remove the chops from the marinade, shaking off excess, and grill until browned, the meat is no longer pink inside, and the meat shows good grill marks, 5 to 8 minutes per side. Brush several times with marinade and let the marinade cook onto the surface of the meat. Discard excess marinade. While the meat is grilling, place 4 pineapple rings onto the grill, and allow to cook until hot and the slices show grill marks; serve the chops topped with the grilled pineapple rings.

raw_recipe.headline: Pineapple Grilled Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Pork chops marinate overnight in a sweet and savory Asian-inspired mixture of pineapple juice, brown sugar, and soy sauce before they're grilled and served with grilled pineapple slices.

review.reviewBody: Due to bad planning on my part, these stayed in my fridge for 48 hours before being grilled tonight. YUMMY!!! Hubby says it's the best pork chop he's had in a long time. Tender, juicy, tasty, extremely easy to put together, this is no brainer for my regular summer rotation. Thanks for posting this keeper. Don't change a thing, it's perfect as is.

I've made this so many times. An absolutely great marinade. Instead of buying canned pineapple, I buy a fresh pineapple, cut of a piece about 1-1/2 inches thick, cut off skin, remove center, throw that and all other ingredients in a blender and voila, marinade. If I think about it I add a small piece of ginger. I make a bit more than the recipe calls for as it makes a fabulous sauce as well. I just thicken it with a bit of corn starch. I grill nice spears of fresh pineapple and baste with the sauce. I have a friend who always asks if I'm making those pork chops. I use nice fat bone-in chops and they grill beautifully. Thank you so much for a great recipe.

I've died and gone to pork heaven. So. Good. I added some ginger to the marinade. Simmered some extra marinade on the stove to reduce, and poured in into the holes in the middle of the pineapple rounds, and felt like an artist. Remember to save a little of the pineapple juice for your Mai Tai.
Delicious. Doubled recipe for 8 pork chops and added 2t of dried ginger. Chops were tender and juicy. Boiled marinade until reduced by half and basted the chops when I turned them.

Best pork chop I’ve made so far! Hubby loved it too. Don’t have a grill, so cooked 3/4” chops 7 min per side on range. Added 1/2 tsp ground ginger, a garlic clove, and a splash of spiced rum to the marinade.

This was great! I made a few changes that suit our situation. Change #1 I did not have pineapple rings but I had a lot of pineapple chunks. Change #2 I need to control the amount of sodium I get daily so soy was out, but I make a soy substitution. Change #4 We use a grill mat that keeps the grill clean. Change #5 I cooked vegetables along with the leftover pineapple in a grill pan. Change # 6 I cooked the remaining marinade and pineapple juice, and added some corn starch for a sauce. 
I think I got the essence of the recipe, but individualized it for our needs.

I was hoping to grill them, but the weather was against me that evening. I also has the chops in the marinade for about 40 hours. I ended up cooking them in my 12" cast iron pan along with the pineapple rings. cooked them to 145° on medium heat so not to burn the sugar in the marinade. came out perfect!

Made this for dinner tonight. Everyone loved it. The only change I made was to use low sodium soy sauce as my father-in-law has dietary restrictions. I had some pineapple chunks in the cupboard so I took some of the marinade, sauteed the chunks, and added corn starch to thicken for a bit of "gravy". Will definitely make this again.

I found this recipe 3 hour before dinner so I only marinaded for 2.5 hrs. My family loved it, even my son who is a picky eater. Also, instead of throwing out the marinade, I made gravy with using 1 tbsp corn starch for my rue.

The longer you marinate the chops the better! One night we planed on making these and the next day decided were getting take out. The Pork Chops were in the fridge and the wife decided to freeze them and make them for another time. Well we defrosted them on the counter to make for dinner and wow what a difference when things marinate longer.

This is an amazing recipe. I however used a Teriyaki baste and glaze and added just a little lite soy sauce to it. Added 1/4 tsp of ginger. I also put lite Soy Sauce and just a little chili powder on the pineapple rings. I marinated the porkchops and the pineapple rings for about 30 minutes. When I put the pork on to grill I added the pineapple rings to the other marinade along with the chili powder and soy sauce, until they were ready to grill. Cooked Asian veggies with them and it was so amazing.!
Excellent and definitely one of our favorite recipes

This is the perfect example of little effort with big reward. I put all ingredients (low sodium soy sauce) plus a few pineapple rings and a bit of ginger, in a blender then pour the marinade over the bone-in pork chop. Marinate overnight, turn chops over in the morning to marinate all day. Served with a side of rice and green beans. A winner every time! I have made with boneless and bone on, the bone on always turns out the most juicy! My kids have enjoyed this recipe from toddler to teen! Only con is it takes planning ahead you need to marinate for at least 8-10 hours, longer is better.
Not only tender but the flavor is incredible.

Nice and juicy results. The pineapple on top makes a great combination. I marinated it over night using the juice from a 16 ounce can of pineapple and was glad I had a little extra marinade. I definitely recommend on marinating at least over night if not 24 hours.
I made it again last night and even after marinating the pork overnight and cooking it to 145 it still ended up a bit dry. I do like the pineapple served with the pork.
like the recipe with 1 exception. Pork Chops should be cooked to an internal temperature of 145°. If you cook them till all the pink is gone they will be dry and tough.
Marinade it as long as you can, it just gets better.
Made these over the 4th of July holiday weekend and they were oh-so-yummy! Didn't change a thing. Kid and husband approved!
